items.title: The exclusive row's 'unique production source' did not match production wiring and omitted alternate injection paths
items.rework: identity-auth/design.md:3616 now reads: sole production source = recovery.DeploymentExclusive in the registered anchor adapter bundle (bundle four ports must be complete, missing one -> ErrAdmissionBinding; empty/unregistered/unusable config path -> all four fall to recoveryClosedPort); root-side sole DeploymentExclusive adapter shape is restoreDeploymentExclusive, which currently has no production construction site; status column states newRecoveryAnchorRegistry(nil) keeps the registry empty so exclusive can only be recoveryClosedPort, and recoveryRootInputs.exclusive is test-only and must not replace the registry source.
items.verification: Verified against cmd/han-server/recovery_sources.go:425-430 (four-field bundle), :455-466 (nil field -> ErrAdmissionBinding), :470-492 (four ports set to one recoveryClosedPort), :523-531 (closedPort asserts recovery.DeploymentExclusive), recovery_runtime.go:551 (newRecoveryAnchorRegistry(nil)), :555 (resolve), :565-567 (inputs.exclusive override), recovery_exclusive.go:13-42 (definition only; rg non-md hits are that file plus recovery_exclusive_test.go).
items.disposition: CLOSED. The coupling of the deployment-lock source to the anchor adapter bundle does not create an unsatisfiable release path: ADR-0030 bounds only the first phase, gap-map:119 already registers S4.23 as a candidate unlock item, the dependency chain S4.23 bundle -> ADR-0032 lock backend/ACL evidence -> formal Task registration -> human production approval is acyclic, production recovery is already closed by recoveryClosedJournalAnchor at recovery_runtime.go:586, and framework.md:1096 states the order checkably. Closure condition 1 requires that the unique production source be listable, not deliverable in this round.

items.title: Lead-added: POSIX filesystem precondition missing from the deployment-lock text
items.rework: All three places now require the lock file to live on a local POSIX filesystem proven to provide reliable OS exclusive-lock semantics, and state that shared/NFS-class filesystems are not claimed to be supported until lock semantics are proven; framework.md:1088 ties this explicitly to the ADR-0019 production FileRecoveryJournal precondition and says it does not extend any support matrix.
items.verification: Compared with ADR-0019 at framework.md:471 (same wording family); no Windows production exception added; no extension of the ADR-0026 Windows SID matrix or the FileRecoveryJournal POSIX matrix; Windows unsupported / exit code 2 retained at framework.md:1088 and identity-auth/design.md:3922.

items.title: The 'test-only' restriction on recoveryRootInputs.exclusive is documentation-only; the override in code is unconditional
items.fact: identity-auth/design.md:3616 and framework.md:1060 state that recoveryRootInputs.exclusive is synthesis/test injection only and must not replace the registry source. In code, recovery_runtime.go:565-567 applies 'if inputs.exclusive != nil { anchors.Exclusive = inputs.exclusive }' with no provenance or build-tag check after resolve at :555. Today no production caller sets the field: rg -n 'exclusive:' --glob '!*_test.go' cmd internal exits 1.
items.impact: The constraint exists only in prose; a future S4.22 assembler could wire the port directly and bypass the single-source rule without any test failing. No current production exposure because exclusive resolves to recoveryClosedPort.
items.recommendation: Add a negative acceptance item to S4.22 (production assembly must not set recoveryRootInputs.exclusive, or isolate the override behind an explicit test-only switch) with a failing negative test. Do not change the design in this round.

items.title: Ordering constraint 9 is not mirrored in the ADR-0032 release-gate list
items.fact: framework.md:1096 places the ordering/source-coupling rule in '不变量与约束' item 9, while release conditions 1-7 at :1100-1106 contain no gate requiring that exclusive be wired into the production root through the registry in a checkable way. Conditions 1-4 concern the lock backend and its evidence and could in principle be satisfied with no registration path.
items.impact: Does not make release unsatisfiable (condition 5 allows an ADR revision or a new decision, and :1096 sits next to the list), but a reader of the release-gate list alone has no checkbox for it, so Task planning could drop it.
items.recommendation: In a later ADR revision or Task registration, add 'single source wired through the registry and checkable via the approval record' to the release-gate list, or mark it explicitly as a sub-item of condition 5.
items.disposition: non-blocking; fold into a later ADR/Task round
